name: Canagliflozin
summary: An SGLT2 inhibitor with proven kidney outcomes in diabetic nephropathy and modest weight loss, but with a lower-limb amputation signal.
mechanism: Inhibits SGLT2 in the proximal tubule, increasing urinary glucose and sodium excretion and lowering the filtration load on the kidney.
pharmacodynamics: Lowers A1c, reduces weight and blood pressure; slows diabetic kidney disease progression (CREDENCE).

pharmacokinetics.onset: Glycosuria within hours of first dose

dosing.adult: 100 mg once daily before the first meal; may increase to 300 mg once daily

contraindications: Dialysis or eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m2 (not indicated)
warnings: Rare euglycemic ketoacidosis — hold before surgery
Amputation signal (mainly toes/feet) and fracture risk
safety.overdose: Volume depletion; supportive care. Hypoglycemia unlikely alone

indications: Diabetic kidney disease with albuminuria (CREDENCE population)
clinicalPearls: CREDENCE established kidney benefit in type 2 diabetes with albuminuria; efficacy persists at lower eGFR than other SGLT2 inhibitors.
Assess feet regularly given the amputation signal; counsel on foot care.
good: Kidney protection in diabetic nephropathy; effective down to eGFR 30 mL/min.
bad: Prior amputation, peripheral vascular disease, or recurrent genital infections.

provenance.notes: Curated from standard endocrinology/pharmacology references. Values omitted where not confidently known — nothing invented.
